# NOBS stack reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_stack_docs.py from stack.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Machine-readable inventory of every language, framework, library, model, and service NOBS uses. Read by humans learning the stack and by coding agents that need to know what this project already standardises on before proposing new code.

**38 entries.** The machine-readable source is [`stack.json`](stack.json); this page is generated from it.

## Rules any new dependency has to clear

- Cross-platform is a hard requirement: shared backend code must run on Linux, macOS, and Windows/WSL2. A platform-only dependency belongs behind an adapter.
- Local-first and privacy-first: prefer a local or on-device option over a hosted service. Do not add a dependency that phones home by default.
- No dependency for something an Apple framework or the Python standard library already solves cleanly.
- Every new integration must declare its data source, permissions, network destinations, retention, failure behavior, and revocation.

## Tank backend (Python)

### ddgs (DuckDuckGo Search) `9.15.0`

*research-tool* — Web search backing the agent's web_search tool.

**Why it is here.** No API key and no account, which keeps the free local core genuinely free.

**Used in.** `app/research_tools.py`

**Worth knowing.** Unofficial scraping clients break when the upstream HTML changes - this is the most fragile runtime dependency in the project.

**Alternatives.**

- **SearXNG** — You want to self-host search on the Tank - strong local-first fit, worth evaluating.
- **Brave Search API** — You need reliability guarantees and can accept an API key.
- **Tavily** — LLM-oriented search results; hosted and paid.

[Documentation](https://pypi.org/project/ddgs/)

### FastAPI `0.141.1`

*web-framework* — HTTP API framework for the Tank: routing, validation, dependency injection, OpenAPI schema.

**Why it is here.** Validates external input with typed models and generates the OpenAPI contract that the iPhone app and dashboard code against.

**Used in.** `app/main.py`, `app/routes/`, `app/dependencies.py`

**Worth knowing.** The dependency-injection system is the part worth understanding: app/dependencies.py shows typed Annotated dependencies, which is the modern idiom.

**Alternatives.**

- **Litestar** — Wanting built-in DI layers and stricter typing; similar performance profile.
- **Flask + pydantic** — A much smaller surface with no async requirement.
- **Django REST Framework** — You want an ORM, admin, and auth batteries included - heavier than this project needs.

[Documentation](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)

### feedparser `6.0.14`

*research-tool* — Parses RSS and Atom feeds for the news tool.

**Why it is here.** Handles the many malformed feeds in the wild without special cases.

**Used in.** `app/research_tools.py`

**Worth knowing.** It never raises on a bad feed - it sets a bozo flag. Silence is not success.

**Alternatives.**

- **atoma** — You want stricter parsing and typed output.

[Documentation](https://feedparser.readthedocs.io/)

### HTTPX `0.28.1`

*http-client* — Async and sync HTTP client for Ollama, Home Assistant, weather, and page fetching.

**Why it is here.** Async support and a pluggable transport, which is what lets tests inject MockTransport instead of hitting the network.

**Used in.** `app/routes/assistant.py`, `app/research_tools.py`, `app/home_assistant.py`

**Worth knowing.** MockTransport is the single most useful testing feature here - see how tests/test_chat.py uses it.

**Alternatives.**

- **aiohttp** — Async-only and you want a websocket client in the same library.
- **requests** — Sync-only scripts; no async support at all.

[Documentation](https://www.python-httpx.org/)

### psutil `7.2.2`

*system-metrics* — CPU, memory, and disk readings for Tank health and optimizer idle detection.

**Why it is here.** Cross-platform system metrics; the optimizer only runs heavy jobs when CPU is genuinely idle.

**Used in.** `app/agent_tools.py`, `app/tank_optimizer.py`

**Worth knowing.** cpu_percent() needs an interval or a prior call to mean anything - a common source of wrong readings.

**Alternatives.**

- **Reading /proc directly** — Linux-only and you want zero dependencies.

[Documentation](https://psutil.readthedocs.io/)

### Pydantic `2.13.4`

*validation* — Typed models for every request and response body.

**Why it is here.** The wire contract in app/schemas.py is Pydantic models; validation at the boundary is a project rule.

**Used in.** `app/schemas.py`, `app/briefing.py`, `app/agent.py`

**Worth knowing.** v2 is a near-rewrite of v1 in Rust - when reading Stack Overflow answers, check which version they target.

**Alternatives.**

- **attrs + cattrs** — You want structuring without the validation layer.
- **msgspec** — Serialization speed dominates; noticeably faster but a smaller ecosystem.

[Documentation](https://docs.pydantic.dev/)

### pydantic-settings `2.15.0`

*configuration* — Loads all NOBS_* environment variables into the typed Settings object.

**Why it is here.** Configuration is centralised in app/config.py by project rule; this makes env vars typed and documented in one place.

**Used in.** `app/config.py`

**Worth knowing.** Settings resolves paths relative to the working directory - which is exactly why tests/conftest.py chdir's into a temp dir.

**Alternatives.**

- **python-decouple** — A much simpler project with no typing needs.
- **dynaconf** — You need layered config files per environment.

[Documentation](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/)

### Python `>=3.11`

*language* — Language for the Tank backend, CI tooling, and deploy scripts.

**Why it is here.** 3.11 is the supported floor because the code uses StrEnum and modern typing syntax. CI exercises 3.11 and 3.12.

**Used in.** `app/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`

**Worth knowing.** Start with the standard library's pathlib, dataclasses, enum, and asyncio - all four are used throughout app/.

[Documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/)

### python-zeroconf `0.150.0`

*networking* — Advertises the Tank over mDNS/Bonjour so devices can find it without a hardcoded IP.

**Why it is here.** Discovery on the local network with no cloud round-trip.

**Used in.** `app/bonjour.py`, `app/main.py`

**Worth knowing.** Registration is synchronous and runs on its own loop - main.py deliberately pushes it to a thread so mDNS cannot block startup.

**Alternatives.**

- **avahi via D-Bus** — Linux-only deployment; not cross-platform.

[Documentation](https://python-zeroconf.readthedocs.io/)

### SQLite (stdlib sqlite3)

*database* — Local store for approvals, proposals, audit events, briefings, schedules, and dream-team state.

**Why it is here.** Local-first: a single file on the Tank, no server to run, no data leaving the house. 14 tables defined in app/agent_schema.py.

**Used in.** `app/agent_store.py`, `app/agent_schema.py`

**Worth knowing.** WAL mode (set in the schema) is why reads do not block writes. Note SQLite cannot add a NOT NULL column without a default - that shapes the migration list.

**Alternatives.**

- **DuckDB** — Analytical queries over the research library rather than transactional writes.
- **Postgres** — Multiple writers across machines - would break the local-first single-appliance model.

[Documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/docs.html)

### trafilatura `2.2.0`

*research-tool* — Extracts readable article text from a fetched HTML page.

**Why it is here.** Turns a page into something a small local model can actually read.

**Used in.** `app/research_tools.py`

**Worth knowing.** NOBS fetches with httpx first and disables redirects, so an allowed public URL cannot 302 into the LAN - trafilatura's own fetch_url would follow it.

**Alternatives.**

- **readability-lxml** — Lighter dependency, somewhat lower extraction quality.
- **Playwright + custom extraction** — The page needs JavaScript to render.

[Documentation](https://trafilatura.readthedocs.io/)

### Uvicorn `0.52.3`

*server* — ASGI server that actually runs the FastAPI app.

**Why it is here.** Standard ASGI server; the [standard] extra brings uvloop and httptools for speed on Linux.

**Used in.** `scripts/dev.py`, `deploy/tank/nobs-api.service`

**Worth knowing.** Understand the ASGI interface - it is the contract between Uvicorn and FastAPI.

**Alternatives.**

- **Hypercorn** — You need HTTP/2 or HTTP/3.
- **Granian** — Rust-based server, worth benchmarking if throughput ever matters.

[Documentation](https://www.uvicorn.org/)

### Wikipedia-API `0.15.0`

*research-tool* — Fetches Wikipedia article summaries for the lookup_wikipedia tool.

**Why it is here.** A cited, stable reference source for the research library.

**Used in.** `app/research_tools.py`

**Worth knowing.** Always send a descriptive user agent - Wikimedia blocks generic ones.

**Alternatives.**

- **MediaWiki API directly** — You need search, categories, or revisions rather than summaries.

[Documentation](https://pypi.org/project/Wikipedia-API/)

## Developer tooling

### Hatchling `build-system requires`

*build-backend* — PEP 517 build backend that packages the app/ directory.

**Why it is here.** Minimal configuration for a simple package.

**Used in.** `pyproject.toml`

**Worth knowing.** The build backend only matters at install time - it is not a runtime dependency.

**Alternatives.**

- **setuptools** — Maximum compatibility with old tooling.

[Documentation](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/)

### pytest `9.1.1`

*testing* — The backend test suite - 249 tests covering routes, auth, tools, and failure paths.

**Why it is here.** Fixtures make the hermetic-environment pattern in conftest.py possible, which is what keeps tests from touching real Tank data.

**Used in.** `tests/`

**Worth knowing.** Read tests/conftest.py first - the autouse fixture explains why every test runs in a temp directory with NOBS_* env vars stripped.

**Alternatives.**

- **unittest** — Standard library only; far more boilerplate.

[Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)

### qrcode `8.2`

*pairing* — Renders the pairing QR code so a phone can claim the Tank without typing a token.

**Why it is here.** The device token is long by design; a QR code keeps first-run pairing bearable without weakening it.

**Used in.** `scripts/pairing.py`

**Worth knowing.** It is a dev/setup dependency, not a runtime one - the API never generates QR codes itself.

**Alternatives.**

- **segno** — Pure Python with no Pillow dependency for image output.

[Documentation](https://pypi.org/project/qrcode/)

### Ruff `0.16.3`

*linter-formatter* — Linter and formatter for all Python, enforced in CI.

**Why it is here.** Replaces flake8, isort, pyupgrade, and black with one fast Rust tool.

**Used in.** `pyproject.toml`, `scripts/dev.py`

**Worth knowing.** The rule set is pinned explicitly in pyproject.toml. Without an explicit select, a Ruff upgrade silently changes what CI enforces - that happened here and produced 61 surprise failures.

**Alternatives.**

- **black + flake8 + isort** — The older split toolchain; slower and three configs.

[Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)

### uv

*package-manager* — Fast resolver; uv.lock pins the full backend dependency graph.

**Why it is here.** Reproducible installs across Linux, macOS, and Windows.

**Used in.** `uv.lock`

**Worth knowing.** From the same team as Ruff. Note dev.py currently installs with pip, so uv.lock is a pin record rather than the install path.

**Alternatives.**

- **pip + requirements.txt** — What scripts/dev.py uses today for the venv install.
- **Poetry** — You want dependency groups and publishing in one tool.

[Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)

## Apple platform

### App Intents

*system-integration* — Exposes NOBS actions to Siri, Shortcuts, and Spotlight.

**Why it is here.** The 'same assistant everywhere' promise starts with Siri on Apple devices.

**Used in.** `NOBS/Intents/`, `NOBSTankMac/AskNOBSIntent.swift`

**Worth knowing.** App Intents replaced SiriKit for most cases - check the date on any tutorial you read.

**Alternatives.**

- **SiriKit Intents** — The older API; App Intents supersedes it.

[Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintents)

### EventKit

*system-integration* — Reads calendar events and reminders for the daily briefing.

**Why it is here.** The briefing is the product anchor and needs the real schedule.

**Used in.** `NOBS/Services/`

**Worth knowing.** Permissions are progressive by product rule - request access at the moment its value is clear, not at launch.

[Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/eventkit)

### FoundationModels

*on-device-ai* — Apple's on-device language model, used for local processing when Tank is unavailable.

**Why it is here.** Keeps the 'Local' processing route genuinely local.

**Used in.** `NOBS/Services/`

**Worth knowing.** Guard the import - it is not available on every OS version the project builds for.

**Alternatives.**

- **Core ML with a bundled model** — You need a specific model rather than the system one.

[Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels)

### StoreKit 2

*payments* — In-app tips and the NOBScloud subscription.

**Why it is here.** Required by App Store rules for digital purchases.

**Used in.** `NOBS/NOBS.storekit`, `NOBS/Services/`

**Worth knowing.** StoreKit 2 is async/await and much simpler than the original API. Test with the local .storekit configuration file before touching App Store Connect.

**Alternatives.**

- **Square / Stripe** — Payments outside the app - already used for web tips.

[Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit)

### Swift 6

*language* — Language for the iPhone app, widgets, and the macOS Tank supervisor.

**Why it is here.** Native Apple development; strict concurrency checking catches data races at compile time.

**Used in.** `NOBS/`, `NOBSWidgets/`, `NOBSTankMac/`

**Worth knowing.** Swift 6 strict concurrency is the big learning curve: @MainActor, Sendable, and actor isolation. See the axiom-concurrency skill.

**Alternatives.**

- **React Native / Flutter** — Cross-platform mobile - rejected here because the app is deliberately Apple-native.

[Documentation](https://www.swift.org/documentation/)

### SwiftUI

*ui-framework* — The entire iPhone and macOS interface.

**Why it is here.** Declarative UI with Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, and reduced-motion support built in - accessibility is a product requirement, not an add-on.

**Used in.** `NOBS/ConversationView.swift`, `NOBS/Views/`, `NOBSTankMac/MenuContentView.swift`

**Worth knowing.** Keep views small and move state into observable models - the project rule exists because large views become untestable.

**Alternatives.**

- **UIKit** — Fine-grained control or older OS targets; can be bridged where needed.

[Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)

### WidgetKit + ActivityKit

*system-integration* — Home/Lock Screen widgets and Live Activities for approvals and briefings.

**Why it is here.** Passive daily context and live tracking of unfolding workflows.

**Used in.** `NOBSWidgets/`

**Worth knowing.** Widgets run in a separate process with a tight memory budget - they read a snapshot file rather than calling the API.

[Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/widgetkit)

### Xcode 27

*ide-toolchain* — Builds and tests all Apple targets.

**Why it is here.** The only supported toolchain for iOS and macOS.

**Used in.** `NOBS.xcodeproj/`, `scripts/build-ios-simulator.sh`, `scripts/test-ios.sh`

**Worth knowing.** Apple builds cannot run on Linux, which is why the iOS CI job uses a self-hosted Mac runner.

[Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/xcode/)

## Website

### @phosphor-icons/react `^2.1.10`

*design-assets* — Icon set for the website.

**Why it is here.** A consistent icon family, so no hand-drawn SVGs or emoji in the UI.

**Used in.** `website/src/`

**Worth knowing.** Import icons individually so the bundler can tree-shake the rest of the set.

**Alternatives.**

- **Lucide** — You prefer a Feather-derived look.

[Documentation](https://phosphoricons.com/)

### pnpm

*package-manager* — Installs website dependencies.

**Why it is here.** Content-addressed store, so disk use stays low and installs are fast.

**Used in.** `website/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `website/pnpm-workspace.yaml`

**Worth knowing.** pnpm's strict node_modules layout catches dependencies you use but never declared.

**Alternatives.**

- **npm** — Preinstalled with Node; slower and larger on disk.

[Documentation](https://pnpm.io/)

### React 19 `19.2.0`

*ui-framework* — The public website at nobsdash.com.

**Why it is here.** Component model for the marketing and portfolio site.

**Used in.** `website/src/`

**Worth knowing.** React 19 adds Actions and the use() hook; older tutorials will not mention them.

**Alternatives.**

- **Astro** — A content site that ships almost no JavaScript - arguably a better fit for a marketing page.
- **Svelte** — Smaller bundles and less ceremony.

[Documentation](https://react.dev/)

### Vite 6 `6.4.3`

*build-tool* — Dev server and production bundler for the website.

**Why it is here.** Fast dev server and a simple production build.

**Used in.** `website/vite.config.mjs`

**Worth knowing.** Dev uses native ES modules while the production build uses Rollup - behavior can differ between them.

**Alternatives.**

- **Next.js** — You need SSR, routing, and an image pipeline.

[Documentation](https://vite.dev/)

## Local AI

### nomic-embed-text

*model* — Embedding model for the research library index.

**Why it is here.** Local embeddings mean research can be searched without uploading it anywhere.

**Used in.** `scripts/setup-local-ai.sh`

**Worth knowing.** Embeddings are how semantic search works: text becomes a vector, and similarity is distance between vectors.

**Alternatives.**

- **bge-m3** — You need multilingual embeddings.

[Documentation](https://ollama.com/library/nomic-embed-text)

### Ollama

*model-runtime* — Runs local language models on the Tank; every model call goes through its HTTP API.

**Why it is here.** The entire local-first promise depends on inference that never leaves the house.

**Used in.** `app/routes/assistant.py`, `app/agent.py`, `app/briefing.py`

**Worth knowing.** Ollama supports JSON-schema-constrained decoding, which this project uses instead of free-form JSON mode - it is the difference between hoping for valid JSON and requiring it.

**Alternatives.**

- **llama.cpp server** — You want maximum control over quantization and sampling.
- **vLLM** — Serving many concurrent users on a GPU - overkill for one household.
- **LM Studio** — A GUI for experimenting rather than a service.

[Documentation](https://docs.ollama.com/)

### qwen2.5-coder:14b

*model* — Code-oriented model for log analysis and the dream-team sandbox.

**Why it is here.** Better at structured and code output than the general 8b model.

**Used in.** `scripts/analyze_tank_logs.py`, `scripts/setup-local-ai.sh`

**Worth knowing.** A 14b model needs roughly twice the memory of an 8b at the same quantization - the constraint is RAM, not disk.

**Alternatives.**

- **deepseek-coder-v2** — Worth comparing on code generation quality.

[Documentation](https://ollama.com/library/qwen2.5-coder)

### qwen3:8b

*model* — Default general chat and agent model.

**Why it is here.** Fits comfortably in Tank memory while still following tool-call instructions.

**Used in.** `.env.example`, `app/config.py`

**Worth knowing.** Model choice is configuration, not code - NOBS_OLLAMA_MODEL swaps it without touching app/.

**Alternatives.**

- **llama3.1:8b** — A general-purpose alternative at the same size.
- **mistral-small** — Worth benchmarking for instruction following.

[Documentation](https://ollama.com/library/qwen3)

## Smart home

### Home Assistant

*integration* — Bridge to smart-home devices; NOBS calls its REST API rather than talking to vendors directly.

**Why it is here.** One local integration instead of one cloud account per device brand.

**Used in.** `app/home_assistant.py`, `app/agent_tools.py`

**Worth knowing.** Home tools are risk-classified: lights and media are one class, locks and cameras another that always needs approval.

**Alternatives.**

- **Matter/Thread directly** — Long-term direction; avoids the Home Assistant dependency entirely.
- **HomeKit via HAP** — Apple-only households.

[Documentation](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/api/rest/)

## Infrastructure

### cloudflared

*networking* — Tunnels the public marketing site out from the Tank.

**Why it is here.** Publishes a website with no inbound ports opened on the home network.

**Used in.** `deploy/tank/cloudflared-nobsdash.service`

**Worth knowing.** Only the marketing site is tunnelled. The API port is deliberately not proxied - a proxy in front of it would make every remote request look local and break the pairing gate.

**Alternatives.**

- **Tailscale Funnel** — You are already on Tailscale.
- **WireGuard** — Private remote access rather than public publishing.

[Documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/)

### GitHub Actions

*ci* — Runs the backend test matrix on Linux, macOS, and Windows, plus iOS tests on a self-hosted Mac.

**Why it is here.** The cross-platform matrix is how the hard cross-platform requirement is actually enforced.

**Used in.** `.github/workflows/`

**Worth knowing.** Hosted runners are metered. If jobs fail in seconds with no logs and no runner assigned, that is a billing or quota problem, not your code - see docs/CI_TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

**Alternatives.**

- **GitLab CI / Woodpecker** — Self-hosting the whole pipeline.

[Documentation](https://docs.github.com/actions)

### systemd

*process-manager* — Keeps the Tank API, dashboard, and tunnel running and restarts them on failure.

**Why it is here.** The Tank is an always-on appliance; services must survive reboots.

**Used in.** `deploy/tank/nobs-api.service`, `deploy/tank/nobsdash.service`

**Worth knowing.** journalctl -u nobs-api is the first command to run when the Tank misbehaves.

**Alternatives.**

- **launchd** — macOS - already used by scripts/install-tank-launchagent.sh.

[Documentation](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.service.html)
